spec.reason: Ranked first because redis-cart is a single-replica stateful service holding cart data, is on the checkout path, and has reach 1.0 across all five flows. A prior 15-second pod_failure made the frontend unresponsive and was aborted, so this tests the distinct recovery behavior of a pod kill rather than repeating an already-known outcome.
spec.hypothesis: While Redis is being replaced, cart-dependent requests will fail or stall across the shop; after replacement, the service should recover and preserve or restore cart availability.

spec.reason: cartservice has one replica, is a shared dependency of checkoutservice and frontend, and reaches every user flow. Prior cartservice pod kills caused high errors across all flows; this brief unavailability test checks whether the error blast radius differs when the pod stays unavailable rather than being immediately replaced.
spec.hypothesis: With cartservice unavailable, cart operations and flows that call the frontend/cart path will fail; the guard is likely to abort before the full 10 seconds elapse.

spec.reason: shippingservice is a single-replica high-risk dependency used by checkoutservice and frontend, with reach 0.4 on view_cart and checkout. Prior delays of 20 ms plus 5 ms jitter and 40 ms plus 5 ms jitter affected checkout without errors (p95 79.7 ms and 139.8 ms respectively); this lower intensity probes shopper-visible slowdown below the guard threshold.
spec.hypothesis: Checkout will slow moderately, while errors remain negligible and p95 stays well below 1500 ms; prior observations suggest the impact will be concentrated in checkout rather than view_cart.

decisions.reason: The redis-cart pod kill completed and the shop recovered in 8.1s; impact was limited to home and product, while cart-related flows stayed near baseline. Peak error rate was 7.7%, and p95 reached 1579.5ms (above the 1500ms guard), but this was an instant fault and did not abort. The cartservice pod_failure is a distinct outage probe with prior evidence of broad impact, and it passes the validator at 10s; the shippingservice delay then adds network-failure coverage.

The cartservice pod_failure was aborted after the guard observed errors above 20%; all five flows reached 100% error, confirming a broad outage, while p95 decreased rather than slowing because requests failed quickly. Recovery took 23 s and cartservice restarted twice; the shop is now healthy, and the remaining shippingservice delay remains a useful, lower-intensity third failure-class test.

The 15 ms delay completed with no errors and no guard breaches, but checkout p95 rose 3.01× (21.6→65.0 ms) and view_cart 2.12×, despite the reported affected_flows being empty. A bounded packet-loss test can probe whether this dependency’s impact is latency-only or also causes shopper-visible errors; the validator confirms it is within caps and policy.
